UDLCO: Pathological autopsy learning outcomes in post publication/presentation peer review of Clinico pathology correlation CPC around autopsy findings in a 48 year old human with clinical complexity

Introduction: 


The patient centred learnings in a global academic medical institution has for centuries been reflected in it's rate of pathological autopsies conducted that over the years have unearthed nuggets of useful information from individual patients that in many instances may have been the first signposting of a new disease hitherto unknown to mankind.

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy

https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41935-018-0093-3?fromPaywallRec=false

To quote:

"The autopsy was not only performed to provide clinicians with the cause of death but to establish the very nature of the pathology which may have been suspected, or to document pathology which was totally unknown during life. From these individual autopsies, the process of systemic analysis of pathologic features with the application of special stains and the addition of increasingly sophisticated techniques culminated in papers in journals. That exercise continues today. One contemporary example of this process which began with the autopsy is the initial cases of a bewildering, catastrophic disease occurring in young men in San Francisco in the early 1980s which we know as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-acquired immunodeficiency syndrome"

Unquote https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6188261/



Coming to the workflow of a particular global Indian institute conducting regular autopsies presented twice weekly in academic sessions, the flipped classroom approach is used for Tuesday posting of the CPC clinical protocol since many decades before some medical educationist even thought of the term for this! https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flipped_classroom#:~:text=Wesley%20Baker%20was%20experimenting%20with,model%20of%20teaching%20and%20learning.

Course & Management
A 48-year-old female underwent renal transplantation at a private hospital for CKD-ESRD (diagnosed in 
2020, basic disease - unknown). Thirty-five days following transplantation, she developed loose stools, low-grade 
fever and was admitted to a private hospital with altered mentation (?preceded by a seizure episode). 
Hyperglycemia and hyponatremia were observed. She was admitted to PGI emergency the next day, required 
endotracheal intubation for altered sensorium and was later shifted to RICU. Chest radiograph and CT thorax 
suggested possible pulmonary mucormycosis, and neuroimaging showed bilateral intracranial lesions 
(?hemorrhagic infarcts). Physical examination suggested surgical site infection. She was managed with 
intravenous liposomal amphotericin-B, vancomycin and wound debridement. Serum creatinine and urine output 
remained stable till demise while thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis and anemia continued to worsen (required 
PRBC transfusions). There was no clear evidence of hemolysis or TMA. She was managed for infective 
endocarditis based on echocardiography at admission, showing 8*5 mm vegetation in PML. Blood and urine 
cultures were sterile, and CSF showed leukocytosis (neutrophilic). On day 4 of the RICU stay, she developed 
shock, and a repeat echocardiography showed RWMA and reduced LVEF (30-35%); antiplatelets could not be 
administered due to thrombocytopenia. Shock persisted despite vasopressor support. Fever recurred, GCS 
worsened, and neuroimaging suggested further deterioration. EEG showed electrical silence (23/11/23), and the 
patient suffered a cardiac arrest resulting in her demise (25/11/23).
Unit’s final diagnosis
 Post renal transplant status (LERRAR – Oct 2023) 
 Diabetes mellitus (?New-onset diabetes after transplantation) with diabetic ketoacidosis
 Disseminated (Pulmonary and cerebral) mucormycosis
 Surgical site infection – Enterococcus spp.
 Infective endocarditis ?fungal
 Inferior wall myocardial infarction
 Severe sepsis, septic and cardiogenic shock
Cause of death
Raised intracranial tension

Thematic analysis of biopsychosocial factors influencing trunkal obesity outcomes in 16 case encounters in Narketpally

 Abstract:


Biopsychosocial Factors in Healthcare complexity Outcomes - A Case Series Analysis

Introduction: This abstract examines 16 cases to understand the influence of biopsychosocial factors on health outcomes. Recognizing the interplay of biological, psychological, and social determinants of health is crucial for effective patient care.
Methods: The cases were analyzed to identify key biological, psychological, and social factors impacting each patient's health journey. The analysis considered the patients' medical histories, social contexts, and reported experiences to understand how these factors might contribute to their current health status and influence their ability to manage their conditions.
Results: Across the cases, common biological factors included diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and renal disease. Psychological factors included anxiety, grief, stress, and the impact of past trauma or loss. Significant social determinants of health included low socioeconomic status, limited education, and challenging life events. The analysis reveals how these factors interweave, creating complex health profiles for each individual. For example, patients with limited education and lower socioeconomic status often faced barriers to healthcare access and experienced higher rates of chronic conditions. Patients who experienced significant losses or trauma were more vulnerable to developing mental and physical health challenges.
Discussion: This case series analysis emphasizes the importance of a holistic approach to patient care. Healthcare professionals must consider biological, psychological, and social factors to provide effective treatment and management strategies. Addressing social determinants of health, recognizing the impact of psychological well-being, and understanding patients' lived experiences are crucial for providing person-centered care.

Keywords: Biopsychosocial, Health Outcomes, Social Determinants of Health, Chronic Disease, Patient-Centered Care

Thematic Analysis of Cases 1-16

This response outlines a thematic analysis of the provided source, "Cases 1-16", demonstrating the steps of thematic coding and subcoding. Finally, learning insights derived from the case content coding are shared.


1. Familiarization with the Data
The first step involves carefully reading through the case studies to get a comprehensive understanding of the content. This initial reading helps identify recurring patterns, themes, and ideas within the text.




2. Generating Initial Codes


Based on the initial reading of the case studies, the following initial codes are identified:●

Socioeconomic Factors: Many cases highlight the influence of socioeconomic factors on health outcomes. This includes factors such as:○
Occupation○
Income level○
Access to healthcare○

Education●
Lifestyle Factors: Cases consistently mention the impact of lifestyle choices on the development and management of chronic conditions. Some key lifestyle factors include:○
Diet and nutrition○
Physical activity○
Smoking○
Alcohol consumption●
Comorbidities: The presence of multiple chronic conditions in a single patient is frequently observed. This highlights the interconnected nature of chronic illnesses. Common comorbidities include:○
Hypertension (HTN)○
Diabetes Mellitus (DM)○
Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)○
Cardiovascular Disease (CAD)●
Mental Health: While not always explicitly stated, several cases suggest a potential impact of mental health on physical health outcomes and vice-versa. This can be observed through mentions of:○
Stress and anxiety○
Depression●
Access to Specialist Care: Several cases involve referrals to different medical specialists. This signifies the importance of a multidisciplinary approach to managing complex cases with multiple comorbidities:○
Cardiology○
Endocrinology○
Urology○
Surgery○
Ophthalmology○
Dermatology (DVL)○
Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT)●
Medical Management and Outcomes: Each case details the provided medical treatments and their outcomes. The variation in treatment approaches and outcomes underlines the complexities of individual patient care. Examples of treatments and outcomes include:○
Medications (e.g. anti-hypertensives, insulin)○
Surgery (e.g. CABG, knee replacement, cataract surgery)○
Lifestyle modifications (e.g., dietary changes, exercise)○
Outcomes ranging from stabilization and ongoing management to morbidity and mortality


3. Searching for Themes

The next step involves reviewing the initial codes and identifying overarching themes. This process aims to group codes that share commonalities and represent broader concepts:●

Impact of Social Determinants of Health: The codes "Socioeconomic Factors" and "Lifestyle Factors" can be grouped under this theme. This emphasizes the significant influence of social, economic, and environmental factors on health.●

Multimorbidity and Complex Care Needs: The code "Comorbidities" highlights the prevalence of multiple chronic conditions in individuals. This theme reflects the challenges of managing complex care needs, often requiring a multidisciplinary approach.●

Interplay of Physical and Mental Health: Although "Mental Health" is not explicitly discussed in each case, its presence suggests a crucial theme exploring the interconnectedness of physical and mental well-being.●

Healthcare Navigation and Access: The code "Access to Specialist Care" points to a broader theme about how individuals navigate the healthcare system and access specialized services.


4. Reviewing Themes

This stage involves revisiting the identified themes and ensuring they accurately represent the data. This step might involve refining, merging, or splitting themes to ensure they effectively capture the essence of the case studies.

5. Defining and Naming Themes
Finally, each theme is clearly defined and given a concise and descriptive name. This step aims to encapsulate the core meaning of each theme:●

Social Determinants of Health: This theme highlights the impact of social, economic, and environmental factors (e.g., income, education, access to healthcare) on health outcomes.●

Multimorbidity and Healthcare Complexity: This theme focuses on the challenges of managing multiple chronic conditions in individuals and the need for comprehensive and coordinated care.●

Mind-Body Interconnection: This theme explores the interconnectedness of physical and mental health, recognizing that these aspects of well-being can influence one another.●

Healthcare Navigation and Access: This theme emphasizes the importance of individuals being able to effectively navigate the healthcare system and access the specific services and specialists they require.

Subcoding

Subcoding helps refine the analysis within each theme by identifying sub-themes and nuances within the data.

Theme: Social Determinants of Health●
Sub-theme 1: Early Life Exposures: This could include exploring how childhood experiences (e.g., socioeconomic status, access to education) can have long-term impacts on health.●

Sub-theme 2: Health Behaviors and Literacy:** This could examine the relationship between health knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors (e.g., diet, exercise, smoking) and health outcomes.

Theme: Multimorbidity and Healthcare Complexity●

Sub-theme 1: Clinical Challenges of Co-existing Conditions:** Exploring how the presence of multiple chronic illnesses complicates diagnosis, treatment, and management.●

Sub-theme 2: Polypharmacy and Treatment Burden:** Examining the challenges of managing multiple medications and the potential for adverse effects and drug interactions.
Theme: Mind-Body Interconnection●
Sub-theme 1: Impact of Stress and Trauma:** Analyzing how stress, trauma, and adverse life events can contribute to physical health problems.●
Sub-theme 2: Mental Health Implications of Chronic Illness:** Investigating the psychological and emotional impact of living with one or more chronic conditions.
Theme: Healthcare Navigation and Access:●
Sub-theme 1: Barriers to Specialist Care:** Identifying factors that might hinder individuals' ability to access specialists, such as financial constraints, geographical location, or lack of referral systems.●
Sub-theme 2: Coordination of Care:** Examining the effectiveness of communication and collaboration among different healthcare providers involved in a patient's care.

Learning Insights
The thematic analysis of these cases reveals key learning insights valuable for medical professionals:●

Holistic Approach to Care: Considering the social determinants of health, recognizing the mind-body connection, and addressing lifestyle factors are crucial for patient-centered care.●

Managing Multimorbidity: Developing effective strategies for managing patients with multiple chronic illnesses is paramount. This involves addressing polypharmacy, coordinating care among specialists, and supporting patients in managing complex treatment regimens.●

Communication and Patient Education: Clear communication with patients about their conditions, treatment options, and the importance of lifestyle modifications is essential for empowering patients to actively participate in their care.●

Health System Navigation: Understanding the challenges patients face in navigating the healthcare system can help healthcare providers better guide and support them in accessing the services they need.

This thematic analysis provides a framework for understanding the key issues and insights emerging from the case studies. By exploring these themes and sub-themes, healthcare professionals can gain a deeper appreciation of the multifaceted nature of health and illness and apply this knowledge to deliver more effective and patient-centered care.

What are the biopsychosocial factors influencing the outcomes of all the 16 cases? Please classify them by mentioning which case numbers demonstrate these factors and in what way did it influence their outcomes

Biopsychosocial Factors Influencing Outcomes in Cases 1-16


The 16 cases presented in the sources demonstrate how a complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors can significantly influence health outcomes. This response analyzes these cases to identify the specific biopsychosocial factors at play and how they may have impacted the patients' journeys.


Case 1 (53-year-old female with Metabolic Syndrome):●
Biological: Diabetes, Hypertension, Hypothyroidism.●
Psychological: Increased anxiety, constant health worries, disrupted sleep due to health concerns and managing family members' illnesses.●
Social: Limited education due to societal norms, role as a housewife, reliance on family support for household tasks due to fatigue.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's psychological distress (anxiety, worry, sleep disruption) could negatively impact her ability to manage her chronic conditions (Metabolic Syndrome). Her social support system (family) might be a positive influence, but their own health issues could create additional stress.
Case 2 (80-year-old male with AKI):●
Biological: Age, Hypertension, Diabetes, Acute Kidney Injury.●
Psychological: The source does not provide specific details about the patient's psychological state.●
Social: The source provides limited social history, mentioning residence in Kamanpet.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's advanced age and multiple comorbidities (HTN, DM, AKI) likely contributed to his poor prognosis and eventual mortality.
Case 3 (45-year-old female with Hypertension, Diabetes, and Hypothyroidism):●
Biological: Hypertension, Diabetes, Hypothyroidism, history of spontaneous abortion and child mortality.●
Psychological: The source mentions past experiences of depression and worry following the death of her child.●
Social: Started working at a young age (10 years old) due to limited education, experienced work pressure and stress leading to a spontaneous abortion.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's history of loss (miscarriage, child death) and early life stressors (early work, limited education) could have long-term psychological and physical health impacts. These experiences might contribute to her current health conditions and influence her ability to manage them effectively.
Case 4 (65-year-old female with Urosepsis):●
Biological: Rheumatoid Arthritis, Hypertension, Diabetes, Urosepsis, history of bilateral knee replacement and C-section.●
Psychological: The source notes decreased appetite due to abdominal fullness but does not provide in-depth information on the patient's psychological well-being.●
Social: Married, reports decreased bowel movements and urinary incontinence impacting daily life.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's physical health is significantly impacted by multiple chronic conditions (RA, HTN, DM). Urinary incontinence and constipation could also have social and psychological implications, affecting her quality of life.
Case 5 (65-year-old female with Heart Failure):●
Biological: Hypertension, Diabetes, Coronary Artery Disease, Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA), Heart Failure, acute kidney injury, gangrene.●
Psychological: Experienced significant stress and grief after her husband's death, leading to unhealthy coping mechanisms (overeating) and weight gain.●
Social: Widowed, responsible for her family after her husband's death.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's experience of grief and loss, compounded by her social circumstances, likely contributed to her unhealthy behaviors and the development of chronic conditions. This highlights the interplay between psychological and social factors in influencing health outcomes.

Biological: Heart Failure, Hyponatremia, Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.●
Psychological: The source does not provide specific details about the patient's psychological well-being.●
Social: Limited information is available on social factors.●
Outcome Influence: The source primarily focuses on the patient's physical health, making it difficult to assess the influence of psychological and social factors.

Not found in the sources.

Social: Lower socioeconomic background, limited education, widowed, lives with her daughter.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's history of significant loss, combined with her socioeconomic disadvantages, likely creates a context of increased vulnerability to both physical and mental health challenges.

Outcome Influence: The patient's history of serious illness (Dengue, Sepsis) and her current acute condition (ARDS) suggest a complex medical situation where biological factors are likely driving her care needs.
Case 12 (75-year-old female with Heart Failure):●
Biological: Hypertension, Diabetes, Chronic Kidney Disease, Heart Failure.●
Psychological: Experienced multiple personal losses (stillbirth, miscarriage, husband's death, brother's death).●
Social: Lower socioeconomic background, limited education, widowed, lives with her daughter.●

Case 13 (45-year-old female with Hypertension, Diabetes, and Hypothyroidism):●

Outcome Influence: This case reiterates the themes in Case 3, emphasizing the enduring impact of early life adversity and loss on both physical and psychological well-being.
Case 14 (60-year-old female with Gouty Arthritis):●

Social: Lower socioeconomic background, illiterate, engaged in manual labor from a young age, history of multiple pregnancy losses, experienced the death of her husband.●

Case 15 (48-year-old female with Motor Neuron Disease):●

Psychological: The source does not elaborate on her psychological state but notes a history of physical trauma when she was pushed down, resulting in a fracture.●
Social: The source provides some family history but does not delve into her social circumstances.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's medical history indicates a complex interplay of physical conditions. The lack of details regarding her psychological and social context makes it difficult to fully assess their influence on her overall health.
Case 16 (74-year-old male with Congestive Heart Failure):●

Psychological: The source does not provide information about the patient's psychological well-being.●
Social: Limited education, started working at a young age (16 years old) as a carpenter, history of smoking.●
Outcome Influence: The patient's social history suggests that his occupation and lifestyle choices could have contributed to his risk for developing chronic health conditions.
Conclusion:
These cases emphasize the interconnectedness of biological, psychological, and social factors in shaping health outcomes. It's essential for healthcare providers to consider these factors holistically when diagnosing, treating, and managing patients' health. Addressing the social determinants of health, recognizing the impact of psychological well-being, and understanding patients' life experiences are crucial for providing comprehensive and patient-centered care.

Abstract:

Biopsychosocial Factors in Healthcare complexity Outcomes - A Case Series Analysis

Introduction: This abstract examines 16 cases to understand the influence of biopsychosocial factors on health outcomes. Recognizing the interplay of biological, psychological, and social determinants of health is crucial for effective patient care.
Methods: The cases were analyzed to identify key biological, psychological, and social factors impacting each patient's health journey. The analysis considered the patients' medical histories, social contexts, and reported experiences to understand how these factors might contribute to their current health status and influence their ability to manage their conditions.
Results: Across the cases, common biological factors included diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and renal disease. Psychological factors included anxiety, grief, stress, and the impact of past trauma or loss. Significant social determinants of health included low socioeconomic status, limited education, and challenging life events. The analysis reveals how these factors interweave, creating complex health profiles for each individual. For example, patients with limited education and lower socioeconomic status often faced barriers to healthcare access and experienced higher rates of chronic conditions. Patients who experienced significant losses or trauma were more vulnerable to developing mental and physical health challenges.
Discussion: This case series analysis emphasizes the importance of a holistic approach to patient care. Healthcare professionals must consider biological, psychological, and social factors to provide effective treatment and management strategies. Addressing social determinants of health, recognizing the impact of psychological well-being, and understanding patients' lived experiences are crucial for providing person-centered care.
Keywords: Biopsychosocial, Health Outcomes, Social Determinants of Health, Chronic Disease, Patient-Centered Care


Current Study limitations:

Narketpally Biopsychosocial Outcomes Triad:
While the provided cases highlight the interconnectedness of biological, psychological, and social factors influencing health, formulating a "Narketpally Biopsychosocial Outcomes Triad" based on these 16 cases presents challenges. This is due to the limitations of the source material:●
Inconsistent Reporting: The cases present information inconsistently. Some cases provide details about the patient's social history and psychological well-being, while others primarily focus on medical history and diagnoses. This makes it difficult to draw consistent conclusions or create a standardized triad from the data.●
Lack of Specific Outcomes Data: The cases often lack detailed information about the specific outcomes related to the identified biopsychosocial factors. While some connections can be drawn, a more robust triad would require concrete data on how these factors directly impact health results for each patient.
To create a more meaningful and generalizable Narketpally Biopsychosocial Outcomes Triad, consider these recommendations:●
Standardized Data Collection: Employ a structured approach to gathering information about biological, psychological, and social factors for each case, ensuring consistency in the data.●
Outcome-Oriented Assessment: Clearly define and measure specific health outcomes for each patient, enabling analysis of how biopsychosocial factors contribute to those outcomes.●
Expanded Case Series: Increase the number and diversity of cases studied to strengthen the generalizability of the findings and provide a broader representation of biopsychosocial influences on health.
By addressing these points, a more robust and informative Narketpally Biopsychosocial Outcomes Triad can be developed.
